name: Velero
description: Protects against destructive velero operations like deleting backups, schedules, and locations.

destructive_patterns.name: velero-backup-delete
destructive_patterns.description: velero backup delete removes a backup and its data.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Velero backup removes both the backup metadata in Kubernetes and the \ actual backup data from object storage. Once deleted, you cannot restore your \ cluster or applications to that backup point. This is irreversible.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - velero backup describe: Review backup contents before deletion \ - velero backup get: List all backups to verify target \ - Consider retaining backups with TTL policies instead of manual deletion

destructive_patterns.name: velero-schedule-delete
destructive_patterns.description: velero schedule delete removes scheduled backups.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a backup schedule stops automatic backup creation. Existing backups \ created by the schedule are not affected, but no new backups will be created. \ If forgotten, this can lead to outdated backups and recovery gaps.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - velero schedule get: Review all schedules first \ - velero schedule describe: Check schedule configuration \ - Pause the schedule instead if temporary

destructive_patterns.name: velero-restore-delete
destructive_patterns.description: velero restore delete removes restore records.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting restore records removes the metadata about past restore operations from \ Kubernetes. This does not affect the restored resources themselves or the original \ backups. However, audit trails of restore operations will be lost.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - velero restore get: List restores before deletion \ - Document restore history externally if needed for compliance

destructive_patterns.name: velero-backup-location-delete
destructive_patterns.description: velero backup-location delete removes a backup storage location.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Removing a backup storage location disconnects Velero from that storage backend. \ Backups stored there become inaccessible to Velero (though data remains in storage). \ You won't be able to restore from those backups until the location is recreated.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - velero backup-location get: Review all locations \ - Verify no critical backups depend on this location \ - Migrate backups to another location before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: velero-snapshot-location-delete
destructive_patterns.description: velero snapshot-location delete removes a snapshot location.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a snapshot location removes the configuration for volume snapshots. \ Existing snapshots may become orphaned and inaccessible through Velero. Volume \ restores that depend on this location will fail.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - velero snapshot-location get: Review all snapshot locations \ - Verify no backups use this snapshot location \ - Migrate to a new snapshot location before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: velero-uninstall
destructive_patterns.description: velero uninstall removes the Velero deployment and related resources.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Uninstalling Velero removes the deployment, CRDs, and all Velero-managed resources \ from your cluster. Backup schedules stop immediately. While backup data in object \ storage is preserved, you cannot restore from backups until Velero is reinstalled \ and reconfigured.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Document current configuration before uninstalling \ - velero backup-location get: Record storage locations \ - velero schedule get: Record all schedules \ - Export Velero resources: kubectl get -o yaml
